page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-16 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 128 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

Operating on the arm64 architecture, this server type leverages the power efficiency inherent to ARM processors, which translates to a favorable qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for memory-intensive workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource contention from neighboring tenants. The absence of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses means network and storage configurations must be provisioned separately, allowing for precise resource allocation.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance appropriate for memory-intensive applications that do not require GPU acceleration or local NVMe drives. Suitable workloads include medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application servers, and data processing pipelines that benefit from a 128 GB memory footprint.
